aliases_help:
Normally, all registers can have address from 0 to 65535. By using of aliases, you can define virtual address fields for every type of registers. Normally:
- discrete inputs are from 10001 to 20000
- coils are from 1 to 1000
- input registers are from 30001 to 40000
- holding registers are from 40001 to 60000

Every alias will be mapped internally to address, e.g., 30011 will be mapped to input register 10. and so on.
alwaysUpdate_help:
Normally, if the value has not changed, it will not be written into ioBroker.
This flag allows updating the value's timestamp by every cycle.
directAddressesExplanation:
Used for binary inputs and coils.
Without this flag the bits will be addressed from like: `0 => 15, 1 => 14, 2 => 13, ..., 15 => 0`.
With this flag activated the bits will be addressed as: `0 => 0, 1 => 1, 2 => 2, ..., 15 => 15`.
directAddresses_help:
Used for binary inputs and coils.
Without this flag the bits will be addressed from like: `0 => 15, 1 => 14, 2 => 13, ..., 15 => 0`.
With this flag activated the bits will be addressed as: `0 => 0, 1 => 1, 2 => 2, ..., 15 => 15`.
disableLogging_help: Suppress connection error messages in the log. When enabled, connection errors will not be logged to reduce log noise.
ignoreTransactionId_help: Only for devices that do not echo the transaction ID of the request (every response is dropped with "Dropped a response with transaction ID"). Otherwise, a stale or duplicated answer can be taken for the wrong request.

padAddressInId_help: Pads the address in the generated ID to the width of the highest address, so that IDs sort numerically: `011_Input` and `119_Input` instead of `11_Input` and `119_Input`.
doNotIncludeAdrInId_help: Do not add address in the generated ioBroker iD. `10_Input10` vs `Input10`.
doNotRoundAddressToWord_help:
Normally, the coils and the discrete inputs addresses are aligned to 16 bit. Like addresses from 3 to 20 will be aligned to 0 up 32.
If this option is active, the addresses will not be aligned.

maxGap_help: Registers within this address gap are read in one request. 0 = read only contiguous configured registers; higher = fewer requests but reads addresses in between. Default 10.
maxGapExplanation: To reduce the number of Modbus requests, the adapter combines several configured registers into one read request even when there are small gaps between their addresses. This is faster, but it also reads the registers lying in those gaps — which are not in your configuration and may not exist on the device. Some devices answer such a request with "ILLEGAL DATA ADDRESS", so the whole block fails to read. This option sets how large a gap (in registers) may be bridged. Set it to 0 to combine only registers with consecutive addresses, so the adapter reads exactly the registers you configured (contiguous registers are still merged into one request). Higher values combine more aggressively and produce fewer requests, at the risk of reading non-existent addresses. Default: 10.
readNotifyExplanation: When running as a Modbus slave, a notification state under readNotify.<register id> is written whenever an external master reads a register. The state is read-only and counts up on each read (optionally with an expire time for watchdog use). The notification is sent after the response has already gone out to the master, so an updated value only takes effect on the master's next read.
notifyOnReadExpire_help: Expire time in seconds for the counter state. 0 disables expiry. Useful as a watchdog to detect when the master stops reading.
